evidence: Walked all 52 scored criteria (40 Functional, 5 Polish, 5 Visual Likert) and both gates against the frozen golden source. For every criterion there is a plausible passing path. FUNCTIONAL. Intake: POST /api/jobs (src/index.js:202-214) refuses a blank title or team, a manager_id that is not a hiring_manager, and a non-integer or out-of-range limit. The UI turns '2.5' into NaN, which becomes null (board.js:72), so 0, 51 and 2.5 are all refused. Add-candidate (index.js:216-233) puts the card at the bottom of Applied and returns field:'candidate_email' for an invalid address (400) or a duplicate in any case (409). The client marks the email field and keeps every input (board.js:52-55). Moves (checkMove index.js:238-265): a skip is refused 409; a Hired reject is refused; a blank reason is refused 400; a reopen goes only to rejected_from; the hiring-manager origin/target rule matches rules.md section 3; a manager of another job gets 403. The version check gives 409, and its message names the last activity line, e.g. 'F was changed by someone else (Mei Lin moved F from Screen to Applied)', which covers hro_stale_refused and hro_refusal_status. Bulk moves (moveCards index.js:274-321) are one immediate transaction ranked by stage index then position, so Y,W,X and A2,V arrive in board order. Interview places are counted for the whole set. Any failing card refuses the whole set, which covers both B(6) and B(10a). Undo (index.js:348-373) requires action.id equal to the latest unundone action, every card version equal to version_after, and room in Interview. It restores the index, rejected_from and reason, and is single-use. A note does not bump the version, and the Down control moves the clicked card itself (board.js:233-238), so B(12) goes ahead and B(14) is refused as required. I traced protocol B (0)-(15) step by step; each expected order and outcome follows. Access: observer 403; candidate 403, or 404 for others (mayMove/staffOnly); anonymous 401 for every route, including /api/bootstrap, which carries the board and Activity. Candidate bootstrap returns only id, job_title, team, status label and thread summary. It carries no notes, reason, rejected_from or position. The SSE stream carries only 'changed'. Activity logs one line per card with actor, stages and the rejection reason; undo lines read 'X undid a move: Y is back in Stage'. It is ordered id DESC, has a job filter, and pages 50 at a time behind a 'Show more' button. Refusals throw before log() or inside a rolled-back transaction. Conversations: messages are rendered with textContent and white-space:pre-wrap; Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and after sending the box is empty and focused with the draft cleared. Paging returns 30 at a time with earlier_count. Unread is computed per user from reads.last_read_id, and sending marks the conversation read. The seen boundary excludes the observer and counts recruiters plus the job's manager. A conversation scrolled up gets a pending '1 new message' pill and no markRead; a view not active never marks read (threads.js:146-160). Drafts live in localStorage keyed hireops.<userId>.draft.<appId>. On a 401, sessionLost() shows sign-in and keeps the drafts. Restart: seedIfEmpty runs only when there are no users, so a restart does not reseed. Seed facts hold: Platform Engineer Applied reads Greta, Ade, Marco and Screen reads Priya, Samuel; Noor's note is present; Lena APP-301 has read_count 2 of 3 with the last message from REC3, so 1 unread; Noor's Platform Engineer conversation is 120 messages, i.e. 30 shown plus 90 earlier; candidate statuses match hro_candidate_view. POLISH: board and thread updates patch keyed nodes in place and restore focus (board.js:321-341, threads.js:36-65), and the message log is the 46vh scroll container with a prepend scrollTop correction (threads.js:168-172). Failed send: fetch rejects, giving status 0, the text 'Not sent. The server could not be reached...', and the box keeps the text. RUNTIME EVIDENCE: scripted golden harness, 26 groups passed against hash-matched frozen bytes with a real restart. I also ran my own client-only Chrome headless probe for the unharnessed scroll-offset leg of hro_pol_live_board (per-row-review/evidence/18/board_scroll_probe.json): window.scrollY stayed unchanged (900 to 900, 1381 to 1381), the details stayed open, and the note text and focus were kept, both when the moved card sat above the viewport and when it sat below. RESIDUAL RISKS (why risk=true): (a) No configured judge run or Oracle score exists (the raw-evidence-index scope says so), so 'the oracle can score high' is not measured. Lessons 17 and 19: the harness does not cover several newer legs: the twelve-card board-scroll leg, failed send with an aborted request, the invalid places values 0/51/2.5, completeness of Activity lines, and note-draft isolation in hro_pol_session_resume. I checked these by source and, for the scroll leg, with the stub probe only. (b) Latent flake in the hro_unread_counts negative leg ('Tomas's next message does not raise his count or total'): on a live update, render() paints the bootstrap's unread=1 into the list and nav badges before the async catchUp() then markRead() zeroes it (app.js:101-116, threads.js:204-214). The window is about one localhost GET; 500 ms polling over 15 s can sample it, an estimated low-single-digit percent chance per run. (c) hro_seen requires 'Move Tomas's page off that conversation (to his applications list)'. The golden candidate view keeps the open conversation beside the list and has no close or back control (the nav has only 'My applications', which does not close it). A judge that only clicks that nav item leaves the conversation open, and the live catchUp marks Rafael's next message read, so the message shows Seen too early. Opening the other application's conversation or reloading avoids this. (d) The golden lowercases candidate emails (index.js:221), so a judge that enters a mixed-case address would see a different email in hro_add_candidate ('matches what was entered'). (e) The full-Interview refusal is shown in a board-level alert that does not name the card. Focus goes to the card's select, which satisfies the stated legs, but a strict reading of 'no reason is shown on or for that card' is possible. None of (b)-(e) blocks a passing path. Each is a bounded chance of the Oracle scoring below 1.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening, none required for this row: (1) Run the full configured judge on the golden and record the Oracle score before upload; add the new legs (board scroll, aborted send, 0/51/2.5, note-draft isolation) to workspace.cjs. (2) In threads.update, apply catchUp/markRead before painting the counts when the open conversation is at its newest message, or suppress unread for the open-at-bottom conversation, so a raised count never paints. (3) Give the candidate view a 'Back to my applications' control that closes the open conversation. (4) Store the email as entered and compare it lowercased. (5) Also show the refusal reason on the refused card.
